summary: SL-077 centralized the previously single-use SetThreadErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS) guard into one thread-scoped struct enforced as the only path through SynchronousIoCancel.Open -- the scanner's single I/O funnel for root, subfolder and SizeProbe opens -- backed by a compile-time-enforced architecture rule and validated end-to-end against two real empty removable drives on this machine. Getting there took 2 rounds each of repro, risk-spike, design, critique and build-slice, and 5 rounds of code-review, largely because the design's own core premise -- that validate could never reach an empty removable drive -- turned out to be false on this exact machine, and because the new architecture rule's path-API name list needed three successive widenings to approach completeness. Two minor findings about that name list (O-026, O-027) remain open and owed to build-slice; the merge gate will refuse until they're closed.

candidates.title: Confirm the pre-fix exe actually raises the disk-prompt box on this machine's real empty drives (E:\, F:\)
candidates.why: Every stage that touched a real empty drive (build-slice #2, validate-slice) showed the fix produces no hang, but nobody has run the pre-fix build (uat 14acea3) against E:\/F:\ because doing so would put a modal box on a person's screen. 'No box after the fix' has never been shown to differ from 'no box either way' -- this card reader might just return error 21 silently regardless of the guard. A person running the pre-fix exe once, ready to dismiss a box, settles whether this slice fixed a real symptom.

candidates.title: Decide whether handle-based calls after media removal mid-scan come into the critical-error scope
candidates.why: Design case C-014 and open_question left this explicitly for a person: listing, GetFileInformationByHandleEx and GetVolumeInformationByHandleW can still hit a 'no disk' box if media is pulled after a handle is already open. Review m1's disposition named the candidate answer (a process-wide SetErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS) at App startup, per Microsoft's own best-practice text) but deferred it as belonging to a follow-up slice.

candidates.title: Single-source the path-API name list instead of hand-copying it across fitness.yaml, ArchitectureRulesTests and the Kernel32 count Fact
candidates.why: The same 3-literal-drift pattern already cost SL-069 and SL-075 a build attempt, and cost SL-077 three successive regex widenings (m2, R2-m2, m1) across 5 code-review rounds -- and two of those findings (O-026, O-027) are still open. A generator or single-source-of-truth for this alternation would end a recurring, review-round-expensive class of finding.

candidates.title: Re-examine whether a fix that modifies SynchronousIoCancel.Open (the scanner's I/O funnel) should auto-raise risk tier the way slices that create the scanner do
candidates.why: Q-002 already established that slices touching the scanner get cut above the default tier for harder review. SL-077 modified the scanner's single open-funnel but stayed medium, which skipped critique-review entirely -- yet the slice needed 5 code-review rounds and its design's central testability premise turned out to be false on this machine.

candidates.title: Run a whole-drive C:\ scan through the published exe with the fix in place
candidates.why: Validate explicitly did not reach this ('not run: 16-thread probe load for minutes on a shared machine'). This is the one perf/regression check for a change to the scanner's single open-funnel that has never been run post-fix, and M2's wrapper may add a second SetThreadErrorMode pair per open on top of the ~37ns already measured.

candidates.title: Run the counting-rule and critical-error-box suite on Windows 10
candidates.why: The project targets Windows 10 and 11, but every stage of this slice (and the ones before it) has only ever run on Windows 11 build 26200. Validate flagged this as not reached.

payload.estimate_error: Opened medium/medium risk with 1 designer, which by this project's own tier policy meant critique-review was skipped entirely. But this slice modifies SynchronousIoCancel.Open -- the scanner's single I/O funnel that every path open (root, subfolder, SizeProbe) goes through, the same class of file Q-002 already flagged as warranting a harder tier when a slice CREATES the scanner. The fix diff itself stayed small (~3 src files), but the machinery around it (the architecture rule, its twinned parity files, and end-to-end real-hardware validation) turned out to be the expensive part: code-review ran 5 times, build-slice ran twice, and the design's own central premise -- that validate could never reach an empty removable drive -- was factually wrong on this exact machine from the start. A harder tier would have forced critique-review to run, which is exactly the kind of check that should have caught an unverified 'cannot be tested' claim before build.

learned.lesson: This dev machine has two real empty removable drives (E:\ and F:\, card-reader slots, Removable/IsReady=False), discoverable in five seconds with [System.IO.DriveInfo]::GetDrives(). Every earlier stage (risk-spike, design, critique) assumed no such hardware was reachable and built an indirect thread-mode proxy test instead of an end-to-end one -- the assumption was wrong, not just unverified.
learned.evidence: The design's coherence_check called the empty-drive case 'recalled, not read... no stage exercised it'; a later code-review round ran DriveInfo.GetDrives() and found E:\/F:\ real and empty, discharged as O-023.

learned.lesson: Bare `dotnet build`/`dotnet test` fail on this machine every time: global.json pins SDK 10.0.100 (net10.0-windows) and only 8.0.425/9.0.318 are installed machine-wide. Every command must go through eng/dotnet.ps1, which bootstraps a repo-local SDK per Q-003 -- this is not a one-off environment quirk, it recurs on every slice that touches build or test.
learned.evidence: repro #1 halted purely on this (exit 145, 'A compatible .NET SDK was not found'); build-check and design both re-documented the same workaround independently.

learned.lesson: The architecture-rule 'twinning' machinery (a rule in fitness.yaml, its Fact copy in ArchitectureRulesTests, a plants.json harness row, and rules-parity's derived counts) is this project's most review-round-expensive pattern. SL-069 and SL-075 already paid for it once each; SL-077 needed three successive widenings of one regex (m2 -> R2-m2 -> m1) across 5 code-review rounds and still has two open findings about the shared name list.
learned.evidence: O-019/O-025/O-026/O-027 chain; build-slice attempt 2 existed only to close findings that landed after build-slice attempt 1 had already passed.

learned.lesson: A `using`-scoped disposable struct is not enough on its own to guarantee an armed guard -- `default(...)` and parameterless `new()` both compile and silently no-op. The fix that actually held was making the underlying CreateFileW P/Invoke private and requiring the scope as a mandatory `in` argument to the one public wrapper, so an unscoped call fails to compile rather than silently opening unguarded.
learned.evidence: Critique M1 cited corefx#35045 and dotnet/runtime#126544 as the exact same mistake happening twice in the BCL; discharged via O-016/O-017 by making CreateFile's wrapper throw/refuse without an armed scope.

learned.lesson: For a Win32 hard-error-box bug on this machine, checking for real Removable/IsReady=False drives belongs at risk-spike time, before anyone designs around 'this can't be tested end-to-end.' The spike here checked the published exe's process/thread error mode on C:\ three times but never checked what removable drives were actually attached.
learned.evidence: published-exe-error-mode-at-root-open spike used explorer.exe launches against C:\ only; the real E:\/F:\ drives weren't found until a much later code-review round (O-023).

missed.what: The design's stated premise -- 'validate cannot reach an empty removable drive,' used to justify accepting a thread-mode proxy test instead of an end-to-end check -- was never checked against this machine's actual drive list. [System.IO.DriveInfo]::GetDrives() shows E:\ and F:\ as real Removable, IsReady=False drives, exactly the shape the bug needs. This surfaced only in a later review round with real contact, after build-slice #1 had already passed, forcing an unplanned validate-slice run against real hardware.
missed.caught_by: a later code-review round that ran DriveInfo.GetDrives() directly (filed as O-023)

missed.what: The critique's own widened regex for the path-open architecture rule (finding m2) still missed the ANSI/EntryPoint-renamed-import escape hatch and this project's own already-used domain APIs -- GetCompressedFileSizeW is already imported via a renamed EntryPoint in TestNative.cs, and FindFirstFileNameW is the call the hardlink counting rule will eventually need. It took two further widening rounds in code-review (R2-m2, then m1) to converge, and two of those findings (O-026, O-027) are still open.

payload.reason: O-026 and O-027 (owed to build-slice) remain open: the shared path-API name list still misses APIs this project already uses (GetCompressedFileSizeW, FindFirstFileNameW) and a third un-parity'd copy of the alternation still exists in FailCriticalErrorsTests.cs. Validate itself recorded 'The merge gate will still refuse while they stand.' The fix code and its behaviour are verified and correct; what's owed is closing these two minor rule-machinery gaps in another build-slice pass before commit can run.
payload.summary: SL-077 centralized the previously single-use SetThreadErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS) guard into one thread-scoped struct enforced as the only path through SynchronousIoCancel.Open -- the scanner's single I/O funnel for root, subfolder and SizeProbe opens -- backed by a compile-time-enforced architecture rule and validated end-to-end against two real empty removable drives on this machine. Getting there took 2 rounds each of repro, risk-spike, design, critique and build-slice, and 5 rounds of code-review, largely because the design's own core premise -- that validate could never reach an empty removable drive -- turned out to be false on this exact machine, and because the new architecture rule's path-API name list needed three successive widenings to approach completeness. Two minor findings about that name list (O-026, O-027) remain open and owed to build-slice; the merge gate will refuse until they're closed.
unknowns: Does the pre-fix exe actually raise the 'insert a disk' box on this machine's E:\/F:\, or does this card reader silently return ERROR_NOT_READY either way regardless of the guard? Nobody has run the pre-fix build against real hardware to find out.

Should handle-based calls after media removal mid-scan (listing, GetFileInformationByHandleEx, GetVolumeInformationByHandleW) be brought into the critical-error scope, and if so, is a process-wide SetErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS) at App startup the right mechanism, per Microsoft's own recommended best practice?
Does this fix hold up under a full whole-drive C:\ scan (2.4M+ opens) for both correctness and the measured ~37ns-per-pair overhead, now that M2's wrapper may add a second set/restore pair per open?
what_went_wrong: repro attempt 1 halted purely on environment (bare `dotnet test` fails because global.json pins SDK 10.0.100 and the machine has only 8.0/9.0 installed machine-wide) before anyone routed through eng/dotnet.ps1, costing a full stage cycle.

The design's central premise -- 'validate cannot reach an empty removable drive' -- was never checked against this machine's real drive list and turned out false; a five-second DriveInfo.GetDrives() check would have caught it before design, but it surfaced only after build-slice #1 had already passed, forcing an unplanned end-to-end validate check and a second build-slice attempt (O-023).

The architecture rule's path-API regex needed three successive widenings across review rounds (m2 -> R2-m2 -> m1) to approach completeness, and two findings from that chain (O-026: missing names including this project's own GetCompressedFileSizeW/FindFirstFileNameW; O-027: a third un-parity'd literal) remain open and still block merge.

code-review ran 5 times on this one slice, the most of any gate on it -- two of those rounds were catching things the initial critique should have caught given the evidence was already available: real drives already on the machine, and a renamed-EntryPoint import already in the repo's own TestNative.cs.

The risk-spike's own no-go verdicts (2 of 3 experiments) were correctly overridden by a person's judgment, but the spike itself never checked for real removable-drive hardware -- the one measurement that would have resolved the design's testability uncertainty from the very first stage instead of the fourth.
